- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk aversion or market panic.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price correction), model often fails to adjust; apply a 3–5 day moving average to anchor forecast near recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to dampen volatility-driven bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model often misreads momentum; apply a 2-period lag correction to avoid double-counting sentiment momentum.
